defects: The print-page framing conflicted with existing zero and negative-number checks.
Endpoint domains, reversed ranges and total output bounds were absent.

The original method-equivalence hint is correct but basic, so its score is 3. Linear cost includes records even when they produce no numbers.

objective: Produce exact sorted squares in linear work without shifting a growing result on every step.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Two-pointer scans and array append/reverse remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Sorted squares is chiefly an algorithm lesson.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Using input order, bounded arithmetic and avoiding repeated shifts transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Sorted bounded integers make an explicit linear goal assessable.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A quadratic revealed approach would contradict the efficiency lesson.

defects: The junior unshifted every square into a growing dense result, adding repeated shifts.
Finite exact-square bounds, frozen input and fresh empty output were unspecified.
Longer-input mutation and empty-array reuse escaped old checks.
rationale: State nondecreasing dense bounded integer input and exact square limits. Junior now appends descending squares and reverses once; reference fills from the back and senior uses equivalent two pointers. Frozen signed extremes, repeated zeros/values, preserved longer input, independent empty output and a larger two-sided case pass. A separately authored merge around the first nonnegative value is accepted. Complexity is reviewed structurally rather than proved by timing.

objective: Reverse literal ASCII vowel occurrences while preserving every non-vowel unit and original case.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: String-to-array traversal and fixed-set membership remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Vowel reversal is primarily a two-pointer teaching exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Unicode boundaries, immutability and amortized inward scans transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A fixed ASCII set avoids ambiguous locale vowel rules.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: No-normalization fixtures prevent modest unintended text changes.

defects: The original brief left accented and non-ASCII letters and normalization ambiguous.
A normalizing implementation passed every old ASCII-only test.
rationale: Specify only literal aeiouAEIOU vowels, exact case and unchanged non-vowel UTF-16 units. Dotted I, accented letters, emoji, combining marks, adjacent vowels and no-vowel strings are checked. Existing reference, junior and senior already agree: grouping untouched surrogate pairs differently does not change the resulting string. The revised hint explains bounded inward movement; the independent collect-and-replace alternative agrees. Linear cost assumes constant fixed-set membership.
